cards.explanation: The answer is that Paul calls himself unspiritual and sold as a slave to sin. Paul says the law is spiritual, then looks in the mirror and says, “…I am unspiritual, sold as a slave to sin.” He doesn't dress it up or hand himself a nicer title. Honest from the very first line, friends, and I respect that.

The answer is False. Paul says the opposite: “I do not understand what I do. For what I want to do, I do not do. But what I hate, I do.” A man who did exactly what he wanted wouldn't be scratching his head like this. Paul is puzzled by himself, friends, and that's the whole point of the verse.

The answer is good. Paul says, “And if I do what I do not want to do, I admit that the law is good.” Think about that, bakers. He's the one stumbling, and he still gives the law a clean report. He doesn't blame the law for his trouble.

The answer is sin. Paul says, “…it is no longer I who do it, but it is sin living in me that does it.” He names sin as the one at work inside him. And the same line shows up again in verse 20, so you can spot it twice in this passage, friends.

The answer is False. Paul says, “for I have the desire to do what is good, but I cannot carry it out.” He wants to do good, and he says so right there. The struggle, friends, is between the wanting and the doing.

The answer is that evil is right there when he wants to do good. Paul says, “So this is the principle I have discovered: When I want to do good, evil is right there with me.” Every time he reaches for good, evil is standing next to him. He has gone around this loop a few times by now, friends, and this is where he lands.

The answer is delights. Paul says, “For in my inner being I delight in God’s law.” Don't miss that, bakers. Right in the middle of all that struggle, there's real joy in him for God's law. That's the part of him that loves it.

The answer is the law of his mind. Paul says he sees “…another law at work in my body, warring against the law of my mind…” So there's a battle going on inside him, friends. One side is the law of his mind, and the other side is working against it.

The answer is True, and it's a heavy line. Paul says this other law is “…holding me captive to the law of sin that dwells within me.” Captive is a strong word, friends, and he picks it on purpose. Notice he describes where it lives, too: within him.

The answer is that Paul asks who will rescue him from this body of death. He cries, “What a wretched man I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?” He doesn't ask who will help him try harder, friends. He asks who will rescue him. Rescue is the word he picks.

The answer is God through Jesus Christ our Lord. Paul writes, “Thanks be to God, through Jesus Christ our Lord!” Notice where it lands, bakers, right after his cry for a rescuer. He points straight to God and to Jesus.

The answer is False, because the statement flipped them. Paul says, “So then, with my mind I serve the law of God, but with my flesh I serve the law of sin.” His mind serves God's law, and his flesh serves the law of sin. It's a tidy summary, friends, of the struggle he's been describing all along.
